To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The hotel industry is a good candidate to apply the theory of asset specificity to the study of outsourcing; (2) The six dimensions of asset specificity proposed by Williamson (1979) and Williamson and Winter (1993) are useful for the study of outsourcing in the hotel industry; and (3) The most relevant dimensions of asset specificity for the hotel industry are site specificity, brand capital and human capital.
the outsourcing of the IT function in the hotel industry has been increasing over the past years and that there are several reasons why this is the case.

the main reasons why hotels outsource are: to focus on core business activities; to gain access to external knowledge and skills; to reduce costs; to reduce risks; to gain access and control over external resources; to increase efficiency and effectiveness; and to improve service quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why firms outsource.
the outsourcing decisions that hotel companies make and the rationale for those decisions.
the outsourcing decision making of hotels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study has provided an insight into how asset specificity may be manifested within the context of hotel outsourcing decisions and that it is a useful concept to consider when making such decisions.
asset specificity is a key determinant of outsourcing decision making, but the nature of the asset specificity is not always obvious and can vary considerably between different types of hotel.
outsourcing is a strategic tool for hotel management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
outsourcing is not a one-size-fits-all solution, but rather, a decision that must be made based on a thorough analysis of a company's specific needs.
outsourcing is not a panacea, but a strategic decision that must be made with care, with a clear understanding of what is being outsourced, and why.

we found that the asset specificities of brand capital and site specificity were the most important factors in explaining outsourcing decisions in hotels, and that they were consistent with TCE theory in this context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
outsourcing decisions are made based on the specificities of the assets involved.
asset specificity is an important consideration for hotel owners and operators, and that it should be carefully evaluated before outsourcing any activities.
the asset specificity of an activity is a key factor in determining whether it should be insourced or outsourced.
